e: Kinesis Data Firehose ingests the streaming payment data and delivers it to the S3 data lake with no servers to manage, and Kinesis Data Analytics analyzes the stream in real time. Data Streams with Lambda needs more custom code, and Glue or API Gateway aren't suited to real-time stream analysis.

Moving the images to EFS gives every instance shared, durable storage, and an AMI-based Auto Scaling group (minimum two instances) behind an ALB with CloudFront improves resilience and performance for the website. S3 can't be mounted like a file system on EC2, an NFS share from one instance keeps a single point of failure, and Global Accelerator isn't a cache.

The most secure cross-account access is for each customer to create an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions that trusts the company's account, so the service assumes it and gets temporary credentials. Long-term IAM user keys or Cognito users add credential risk.

A Transit Gateway in the networking team's account (shared to the other accounts via AWS RAM) connects hundreds of VPCs in a hub-and-spoke design with simple routing, far easier than a mesh of peering connections or a transit VPC with VPNs. Internet routing is insecure.

The nightly batch jobs are fault tolerant (a failed job is reprocessed on another instance) and run only 6 hours a day, so Spot Instances in the Auto Scaling group are the cheapest. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances commit to 24/7 usage, and larger instances cost more.

Generating S3 presigned URLs lets users upload straight from their browsers to S3, bypassing the application servers, so uploads scale almost without limit during demand spikes. Uploading through application servers or file gateways/EFS creates bottlenecks.

An Aurora MySQL global database (primary Region with read replicas in each Region, replication typically under a second) keeps a single globally consistent primary reservation database with low-latency regional reads. DynamoDB global tables would require rewriting the application and aren't single-primary, and RDS cross-Region replicas or custom sync are slower or complex.

An EC2 AMI lifecycle policy (Data Lifecycle Manager) or an AWS Backup plan can run twice daily on tagged instances and automatically copy the backups to us-west-2, giving at most 12 hours of data loss with minimal administration. Copying on demand or via custom Lambda is manual or extra effort.

Security groups only have allow rules, so a deny for specific IPs requires a network ACL. The illegitimate requests hit the ALB in the public subnets (web tier), so add the inbound deny rule on the web tier subnets' network ACL.

A cross-Region VPC peering connection with updated route tables lets the eu-west-1 applications reach the ap-southeast-2 databases privately. Security group rules can't reference security groups across Regions, so the database security group must allow the application servers' IP addresses. Transit Gateway peering attaches to transit gateways, not VPCs directly, and still can't use cross-Region security group references.

Aurora Serverless (on-demand, auto-scaling) PostgreSQL-compatible databases scale down or pause when idle, so developers pay only while environments are used (about half of each workday), which beats always-on provisioned databases. S3 Select isn't a PostgreSQL database.

AWS Config can find untagged resources across accounts, which can then be tagged programmatically so that a tag-based AWS Backup plan automatically covers all resources, with little ongoing effort. Manual reviews or Inspector don't ensure everything is backed up.

A static S3 website with Lambda functions triggered by uploads resizes images automatically, stores them in S3, and scales and stays highly available with no servers, which fits unpredictable traffic. EC2-based designs are less scalable, and RDS isn't suitable for images.

With the EKS endpoint private only and nodes in private subnets, the nodes need a private path to the control plane and AWS services, which interface VPC endpoints provide (for example, EC2, ECR, S3, and STS endpoints). IAM permissions and outbound security group rules don't create that network path, and public subnets would violate the design.

Redshift offers a Data API for accessing data from traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications, supports client-side and server-side encryption, and suits analytics workloads (including pausing the cluster outside the hours when it's needed). It isn't a cache and doesn't scale to tens of millions of requests per minute like a serving database.

API Gateway with Lambda using provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments warm for consistent low latency, and both services are fully managed, so it has the least operational overhead. Reserved concurrency only caps or reserves capacity and still has cold starts, and ECS or EKS need more management.

Session Manager has built-in preferences to send session logs directly to an S3 bucket, so enabling S3 logging in the Systems Manager console is the simplest, most efficient way. The CloudWatch agent or custom documents add extra steps.

RDS storage autoscaling automatically increases allocated storage when free space runs low, with no downtime and almost no effort. Changing instance size, moving to Provisioned IOPS, or restoring from backup involve downtime or more work.

AWS Service Catalog lets the company centrally create, manage, and share approved products (such as CloudFormation-based solutions) that customers deploy themselves for self-service. Raw CloudFormation templates, Systems Manager templates, or Config items don't provide a managed self-service catalog.

With unpredictable traffic and moderate-to-high throughput, DynamoDB on-demand mode with the Standard table class scales automatically and avoids over-provisioning or throttling. Standard-IA is for rarely accessed data, and provisioned mode with a capped auto scaling risks throttling.

Cross-account IAM roles are the most secure option: each business account creates a role (BU_ROLE) with DynamoDB access that trusts the inventory application's role, and the application assumes it through STS for temporary credentials. IAM user keys, Secrets Manager, or ACM aren't used to authenticate to DynamoDB.

Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (using the Kubernetes Metrics Server) scales the number of pods with the workload, and the Cluster Autoscaler adds or removes nodes to fit them, together scaling EKS in and out with little operational overhead. Lambda scripts, API Gateway, or App Mesh don't scale the cluster.

Athena Federated Query with the DynamoDB connector queries multiple DynamoDB tables using SQL without custom code, and reads don't affect the application's baseline throughput in the application path, with minimal operations. AppSync, Lambda@Edge, or API Gateway with Lambda require building the data access layer.

Athena can query CloudTrail logs directly in S3 with SQL (for example, filtering errorCode for AccessDenied and Unauthorized), with no custom scripts or ETL. Glue or Batch scripts and QuickSight dashboards take more effort.

The AWS Cost Explorer API provides programmatic access to current-year usage costs and cost forecasts (up to 12 months ahead), so the dashboard can call it directly with little overhead. CSV downloads and Budgets delivery through FTP or SMTP aren't programmatic APIs or forecast data sources.
